final_rationale: The verdict does not change. No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor narrowed and corrected the interpretation of the existing record. That clarification is useful, but it confirms rather than cures the original defect. The admissible evidence still shows that the below-target insurance claims triage segment remains exposed, while the only risk-acceptance evidence is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line and no mention of that exposure. Under the stated policy, monitored rollout, rollback, and post-launch measurement can mitigate only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. That predicate remains unmet. The Actor's narrowed position may justify better disclosure language, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the unresolved issue is not merely a disclosure caveat; it is a missing launch-authorization condition under policy.
remaining_concerns: The affected insurance claims triage use case remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no reviewed and approved risk acceptance that explicitly addresses the insurance claims triage exposure.
The governing policy requires exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance for rollout controls and monitoring to mitigate this weakness.
Disclosure, monitoring, rollback, and a 9% rollout satisfy disclosure/governance considerations but do not satisfy the policy predicate for launch authorization.
